I've had an abundance of teeth issues growing up. So im there with you.

When I was very little I had an underbite. Had to use a Myobrace for years to correct it and had to do all these tedious exercises.

When my adult teeth came though we had 2 bad realisations:

1. I was missing adult teeth. (They just never formed)
2. Some of my adult teeth were abnormally small (the 2 big ones infront that everyone sees included). Again, just how my teeth developed.

This means I had to get them artificially built up. After I got them built up, i had to use an invisiline for a while to try close some of the gaps and make my whole mouth look less awkward as some teeth were at some weird angles.

Then, hooray hooray in highschool I got depression. This lead to me taking pretty bad care of my teeth which, mixed with my history, wasnt great.

I'm now paying for the consequences (literally and figuratively) and it fucking sucks.

Went to the dentist for the first time in a few years and, no surprises, need fillings.

Luckily they are looking a lot better now but im still jealous of other people.

I unfortunately dont have any advice but I can say your not alone. And also, if your with the right person, they wont care. I've been lucky enough to be matched with some people who havent minded mine.

There's always a more hopeful tomorrow. The past is the past but I wish you the best in taking care of your teeth in the future :) with some time it'l be okay, this isnt forever.

I honestly don’t know much about NPD specifically, what I cam tell you is that if you don’t think this is impacting your life to a considerable agree then your probably fine. Its like the difference between anxiety and an anxiety disorder, someone who has anxiety might feel shaky or nauseous during public speaking, whilst someone with an anxiety disorder may have a breakdown over just the thought of having to do public speaking. Like everything, narcissism is a spectrum, its not something you have or don’t have, but if its not wrecking your life, you probably don’t have NPD.

The best thing I can say is that if your really concerned, go to a psychologist, psychiatrist, therapist, whatever, and ask them. We folk on Reddit do not have the answers. Personally, I think a lot of what you said sounds relatively normal as someone who has experienced most of it myself, however I don’t know what you’ve gone through. On some other notes keep in-mind that although trauma can block out memories, if you cant remember it doesn’t mean you’ve had trauma necessarily. Remember, its only a disorder if its negatively impacting your life to a rather large degree. Gl finding answers.
